title: datagen ruleset module
description: One module of a datagen ruleset — the spec sheet the generators read. This schema DESCRIBES the format as it exists (2026-07-31): permissive about domain keys (any module may invent its own vocabulary) but strict about the value shapes the framework recognises everywhere, at any depth. Hover a key for its meaning. Recipes: datagen/AUTHORING.md. Where this vocabulary is heading: datagen/TYPES-PROPOSAL.md.

version.description: Ruleset version, stamped into every build's run.json.

scale.description: How big the generated world is. `members` is the default population when --n is not passed.

history.description: The calendar the world lives on: how far back history goes, and the flagship event's anchor date.

startYear.description: First year of generated history. The most-shared value in the ruleset — many modules read it, so moving it moves everything.

statusMix.description:
Target distribution of member statuses, with its tolerance. Validator-only — nothing generates from it.

NAME TRAP: despite the -Mix suffix this is a Target (target[] + tolerance), NOT a Mix (weighted options for a dice roll). It is the one key whose suffix lies, which is why the schema special-cases it. Rename candidate — see TYPES-PROPOSAL.md.

target.description: Shares per status. Only target[0] (active-ish) is gated; the rest are indicative.

latents.description: Parameters of the hidden per-member dials (engagement, affluence) and how they drift year to year. EXPERT: changing these re-shapes every downstream behaviour at once.

texture.description: Year-to-year wobble that keeps aggregate series from looking machine-smooth. EXPERT.

regimes.description: Eras that bend the world while active (e.g. covid). Applied AFTER calibration, so an era cannot be averaged away — the tide, not the boats.

cohorts.description: Renewal-cycle composition: what share of members sit on anniversary cycles rather than the calendar year, and how many auto-renew.

geography.description: Regional composition of the membership, and the city/state banks members are drawn from.

orgs.description: Employer organisations: how many exist relative to members, and their lifecycle events (acquisition, closure) which feed causal arrows.

prospects.description: Non-members the association knows about — a Person row with no membership extension.

funnel.description: The pre-membership history of recent joiners, so a conversion rate is computable from the data.

membership.description: The renewal engine: the population target and its band, tiers, dues, cancellation rules, and the causal arrows that decide who renews.

events.description: Conferences, workshops and webinars: how many, how well attended, and no-show behaviour.

orders.description: The money chain: products, prices, payment timing profiles, refunds.

committees.description: Governance: the committee catalog, terms, volunteering, seats, meetings, motions and votes.

forms.description: Surveys and the public membership application, including the model that answers them.

tasks.description: Action items spawned by committee meetings and renewal outreach.

issues.description: Support tickets: types, statuses, severity/priority mixes, assignment and comment threads.

messaging.description: Secure member↔staff message threads derived from issues.

relationships.description: The identity graph: employment edges and authored story edges.

programs.description: Certifications, competition entries and advocacy actions.

contacts.description: Contact methods and addresses as first-class bizapps-common rows, including the per-country street/city/postal banks that keep addresses from reading as fake.

platform.description: MJ platform residue: staff users, saved views, queries, lists, notifications, seeded conversations.

sonar.description: The engagement scoring model: factors, weights, bands and time windows. Definitions only — Sonar's own engine computes the scores.

defects.description: Deliberate, labelled data-quality defects with ground truth, so a demo can show finding them.

motifs.description: Authored member archetypes (rising star, quiet fade) stamped onto the anonymous crowd.

heroes.description: The pinned people whose stories a demo script can rely on. APPEND-ONLY: position is load-bearing, because heroes overwrite crowd slots by index — reordering this array rewrites unrelated people.

node.description: Applied at EVERY depth: the value-shape rules keyed by name, plus recursion into objects and arrays. This is what makes `events.registration.attendShare: 45` an error and not just a number.

^\\$.description: Commentary — any key starting with $ is ignored by the generator. $note (why this value is what it is), $comment (module-level), $source / $evidence (provenance), $assumption, $persona. House rule: every authored constant carries one, and a guess says ESTIMATE.

^(?!statusMix$).*([Ww]eights|[Mm]ix)$.description: Mix — weighted options for one dice roll. Weights must be positive and need not sum to 1. Canonical form is an object map { "Gold": 0.05, "Silver": 0.1 } (decided 2026-07-31); the older pair-array form [["Gold", 0.05], …] still appears and is still accepted. A $note may sit alongside the options.

^(?!.*([Dd]ays|[Cc]ount|[Ww]eight|[Yy]ea.description:
Share — a population fraction in [0, 1]. If you meant a percentage, divide by 100: 0.105, not 10.5.

Two legal forms, and the difference is meaningful:
 • a bare number — the generator uses it, nothing checks the result
 • { target, tolerance } — the generator uses it AND the validator gates the generated data against it. Write this form whenever the number is a promise about the output.

anyOf.description: A vector of shares, when the thing has several categories.

^catalog$.description:
CATALOG — what exists in this domain. Lists only: the committees, the products, the courses, the standing agenda, the text banks a generator picks from. If it is a thing rather than a quantity, it goes here.

One of the four sections every block uses: catalog · params · effects · mixes.

(An ARRAY here is the pre-restructure meaning of the word — `programs.certifications.catalog` is a plain list. That resolves itself when a block moves to the four-section shape, where it becomes `catalog.certifications`.)

^params$.description:
PARAMS — every scalar the generator reads for this domain, flat and in one place, so you can see all the knobs at once and a dead one stands out.

A bare number is used but unchecked; a { target, tolerance } pair is used AND gated by the validator. Put a $note beside anything a reader would otherwise have to guess at.

One of the four sections every block uses: catalog · params · effects · mixes.

^effects$.description:
EFFECTS — who differs from the average, and by how much. Flat keys of the form <decision>.<driver> (e.g. "attendance.engagement"), so every effect in a domain is visible on one screen instead of buried inside the decision it modifies.

Each effect declares exactly ONE magnitude form and states a reason. Same rules as the older `arrows` blocks, which this replaces.

One of the four sections every block uses: catalog · params · effects · mixes.

^mixes$.description:
MIXES — weighted options, one dice roll each. Object maps only: { "yes": 0.8, "no": 0.1 }. Weights must be positive and need not sum to 1.

One of the four sections every block uses: catalog · params · effects · mixes.

.*[Tt]olerance$.description: Tolerance — how far the validator lets a generated value drift from its target, in the target's own units (0.02 = two percentage points for a share). Half of a Target pair; the other half is the target-ish sibling. Zero is never right — it would fail on ordinary sampling noise.

.*[Mm]ultiplier$.description: Multiplier — scales a value while a regime is active (0.5 halves it, 1.7 raises it by 70%). Applied after calibration.

.*([Dd]ays|[Mm]onths|[Hh]ours|[Yy]ears)(.description: Window — a duration whose UNIT IS IN THE KEY NAME (…Days / …Months / …Hours / …Years), so no duration is ever ambiguous. A single number, or a two-element [lo, hi] range the generator draws inside.

.*[Bb]eta$.description: Beta — the strength of a causal effect, in log-odds per standard deviation of the driver (0.55 ≈ +4 points at a 50% base rate). Prefer declaring effects inside an `arrows` block, where evidence is required.

.*[Cc]ount$.description: Count — an exact number of rows the generator must stamp (usually an authored defect or motif population). Treated as 'up to' where the eligible pool is smaller.

^arrows$.description: Arrows — the causal rules of this block: who differs from the population average, and by how much. Each arrow declares exactly ONE effect form and carries its evidence.

^years$.description: The calendar years a regime is active.

anyOf.description: A TARGET PAIR, recognised by its shape rather than its name: any object carrying both `target` and `tolerance` is a promise the validator checks. This is why the four-section shape writes gated numbers as pairs — the structure says 'this is enforced' without depending on what it is called.

tolerance.description: How far the generated data may drift from `target`, in the target's own units. Never 0 — that fails on ordinary sampling noise.

n.description: Draw-pool size, which enables the validator's standard-error cushion.

se.description: How many standard errors of cushion to allow. Default 3.

arrow.description:
One causal rule. Declare exactly ONE effect form, plus evidence:
 • liftPts — 'this group is N percentage points higher' (the human form)
 • groupTarget — 'this group lands at N%' (the human form)
 • strength + sign — qualitative ('med', '+')
 • beta — log-odds per SD (the expert form)
 • logitShift — a raw additive shift
The compiler solves the human forms into a beta against the population target, so authoring in points is not a lesser option — it is the recommended one.

liftPts.description: Percentage points this group differs by, measured at the population base rate. Negative for a drag.

groupTarget.description: The rate this group should land at, as a probability (0.62, not 62).

sign.description: Direction of a qualitative arrow. Requires `strength`.

beta.description: Log-odds per standard deviation of the driver. The expert form — prefer liftPts unless you think in log-odds.

logitShift.description: A raw additive shift in log-odds space.

share.description: Prevalence of the affected group, used to solve a human form into a beta. Required in practice whenever liftPts or groupTarget is used.

feature.description: Declarative driver — { from: 'self', field } or { from: 'self', where: {…} } — naming what this arrow keys off.

note.description: Why this effect exists and why this size. One of note / evidence / $note is required: an arrow without a stated reason is an unfalsifiable claim about the world.

evidence.description: Provenance for the magnitude. Say ESTIMATE plainly when it is a guess.

label.description: Plain-language restatement of the magnitude ('med', 'med-strong') recorded alongside a beta, so a reader who doesn't think in log-odds can still tell how big the claim is. Documentation only — nothing reads it.

hero.description: A pinned person: authored facts that survive every dice roll, plus `pins` the validator asserts on their generated data.

memberNumber.description: Identity key, e.g. ICF-000101. Every generator that pins this hero looks them up by it.

title.description: Job title. null is legal and meaningful — an independent or unemployed hero.

employerName.description: null means this hero has no employer, and no organisation row is created for them.

region.description: NA / EU / RoW — must match a region in geography.mix.

theta.description: Pinned engagement dial — never drawn. Higher means more of everything (renewals, attendance, volunteering).

thetaByYear.description: A pinned engagement ARC keyed by year string, for heroes whose story is a trajectory rather than a level (a rising star, a quiet fade).

joinDate.description: Absolute join date. Declare exactly one of joinDate / joinYearsAgo / joinDaysBeforeRelease.

joinYearsAgo.description: Join date relative to the release, in years (pairs with anniversaryOffsetDays).

joinDaysBeforeRelease.description: Release-relative join, so a cold-start story survives any release date.

lapseYear.description: Pins a NO at that year's renewal decision.

employerEvent.description: { year, kind } — a lifecycle event on this hero's employer, which is what feeds the employerEvent arrow.

committees.description: Declared seats: { committee, role, terms[] }. `committee` must name an entry in committees.list — the linter checks the spelling, because a typo silently produced no seat at all.

issues.description: Authored support tickets: { type, title, daysBeforeRelease, detail? }.

certifications.description: Declared credentials: { key, status, enrolledOn, awardedOn? }. `key` must exist in programs.certifications.catalog.

staleEmployer.description: { trueEmployerName, monthsAgo } — deliberately creates a labelled stale-employer defect on this hero.

pins.description: Assertions the VALIDATOR enforces on this hero's generated data — a promise a demo script can rely on. (Two are also read by generators: formResponse and duplicateOf.) Add a pin for every fact your demo will say out loud.
